## Specification (BDD)
- **Title**: Win on all safe cells revealed
- **Description**: Session is won when every non-mine cell is revealed; remaining unrevealed mines are auto-flagged.
- **Scenario**: Given an in-progress game When the last non-mine cell is revealed Then status becomes won, ended_at is set, and every unrevealed mine cell becomes flagged.

## Interface promised to the application layer
The application calls these public methods on this class by exactly these names and keyword arguments (they do not exist yet unless the API above shows them):
- Action `start_game`: params [`difficulty`] — Discards any current board and timer and sets up a new board for the chosen difficulty (Beginner, Intermediate or Expert) with rows, columns and mine_count taken from that difficulty, status ready, elapsed_seconds 0, flag_count 0, no started_at or ended_at, and no mine layout fixed yet; allowed in any status.
- Action `reveal_cell`: params [`row`, `column`] — On the first reveal of a ready game, places mines avoiding the target cell and its neighbours, sets started_at, and moves the game to in_progress; then reveals the hidden, unflagged target cell, expanding zero-count regions, and may end the game as lost (on a mine) or won (when all safe cells are revealed); ignored if the game is won or lost, the position is outside the board, or the cell is already revealed or flagged.
- Action `toggle_flag`: params [`row`, `column`] — Cycles a hidden cell to flagged (flag_count increases by one) or a flagged cell back to hidden (flag_count decreases by one), without starting the timer; allowed only while the game is ready or in_progress, and ignored for revealed cells or positions outside the board.

- Field `cells[].state` holds exactly one of: "hidden" (Cell not yet revealed and not flagged; default state.); "revealed" (Cell has been opened; shows a mine or an adjacency count.); "flagged" (Player marked the hidden cell as a suspected mine.)

    # cells where some are revealed and some flagged.

    game.status = "ready"
    game.mine_count = 10
    game.flag_count = 0

    assert game.ended_at is None

    game.started_at = STARTED
    game.elapsed_seconds = 0
    game.mine_count = 10
    game.flag_count = 0

    assert game.flag_count == 0
    assert game.started_at == STARTED
    assert game.elapsed_seconds == 0

## The other rules of this class
Each of these has its own test, written by someone else at the same time, and one implementation must satisfy all of them at once. They all hold in the situation you arrange, whether or not your scenario mentions them:
- Adjacency count: Given a game with mines placed and a safe cell at a position When the mine layout is fixed Then the cell's adjacent_mine_count equals the number of mines in its up to eight neighbouring cells.
- Zero expansion: Given a hidden cell with adjacent_mine_count 0 in an in-progress game When the player reveals it Then all its neighbouring hidden cells are revealed and any neighbour with count 0 continues the expansion recursively.
- Zero expansion stops at numbered cells: Given a zero-count reveal that reaches a neighbour with count greater than 0 or a flagged neighbour When expansion runs Then that neighbour is revealed only if hidden and not flagged, and expansion does not continue beyond it.
- First-click safety: Given a game in ready status When the first cell is revealed Then mines are placed so that the revealed cell and all its neighbours have has_mine false, and the layout is fixed.
- Flag placement on hidden cells: Given an in-progress game and a hidden cell When the player flags it Then the cell state becomes flagged and flag_count increases by one; Given a revealed cell When the player flags it Then the board is unchanged.
- Flag removal: Given a flagged cell in an in-progress game When the player removes the flag Then the cell returns to hidden and flag_count decreases by one; Given a flagged cell When the player attempts to reveal it Then the cell remains flagged and is not revealed.
- Right-click cycle: Given a hidden cell When the player right-clicks it Then it becomes flagged; Given a flagged cell When the player right-clicks it Then it becomes hidden; Given a revealed cell When right-clicked Then it is unchanged.
- Mine counter may go negative: Given a game with mine_count M and flag_count F When the counter is displayed Then it shows M minus F, including negative values when F exceeds M.
- Loss on mine reveal: Given an in-progress game When the player reveals a mine Then status becomes lost, ended_at is set, all mine cells are shown as revealed, and flagged cells without mines are marked as wrong.
- Terminal state rejects changes: Given a game in won or lost status When the player reveals or flags any cell Then the board and status are unchanged; When the player restarts Then a new game is created.
- Timer starts on first reveal: Given a game in ready status When the first cell is revealed Then started_at is set and elapsed time begins; Given a game in ready status When a flag is placed Then the timer does not start.
- Timer stops at session end: Given an in-progress game When the session is won or lost Then elapsed_seconds is fixed at the value at that moment and no longer increases.
- Timer display cap: Given elapsed time greater than 999 seconds When the timer is displayed Then it shows 999.
- Invalid operations ignored: Given any game state When the player reveals a revealed cell, acts after game end, or targets a position outside the board Then the board and session state are unchanged.
- Restart resets session: Given a game in any status When the player starts a new game at a chosen difficulty Then a new board is created with status ready, elapsed time zero, and no mine layout fixed.
- Board edge boundaries: Given a cell on the board edge or corner When adjacency is computed Then only neighbours inside the board are counted, giving fewer than eight neighbours.

"""
Domain Model: Game (Aggregate Root)
Single Responsibility Principle (SRP) compliant domain model.
"""

from __future__ import annotations
import math
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, date, timezone, timedelta
from typing import Optional, List, Dict, Any, Union, Set, Tuple, Callable
import random


try:
    from src.domain.exceptions import DomainError, StaleDataError, InvariantViolation, MaintenanceRequiredError, MaintenanceLockoutError, ReservationConflictError, BusinessRuleViolation
    from src.domain.events import DomainEvent, MaintenanceRequiredEvent, MaintenanceLockedEvent

        from domain.events import DomainEvent, MaintenanceRequiredEvent, MaintenanceLockedEvent
    except ImportError:

DIFFICULTY_SETTINGS: Dict[str, Tuple[int, int, int]] = {
    "Beginner": (9, 9, 10),
    "Intermediate": (16, 16, 40),
    "Expert": (16, 30, 99),
}
class InvalidActionError(Exception):
    """Raised when an action is refused because the game has ended."""


@dataclass
class Game:
    """Game.

    cells: the Cell records this Game owns, one dict each with the keys id (str), row (int), column (int), has_mine (bool), adjacent_mine_count (int), state (str).
    """
    id: str
    difficulty: str = "Beginner"
    status: str = "ready"
    started_at: Optional[str] = None
    ended_at: Optional[str] = None
    elapsed_seconds: int = 0
    mine_count: int = 10
    flag_count: int = 0
    cells: List[Dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)
    events: List[Any] = field(default_factory=list)

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            k: v for k, v in self.__dict__.items() if not k.startswith("_")
        }

    def start_game(self, difficulty: str) -> None:
        """Discard the current session and set up a fresh board.

        Args:
            difficulty: One of Beginner, Intermediate or Expert.
        """
        rows, columns, mines = self._settings_for(difficulty)
        self.difficulty = difficulty
        self.status = "ready"
        self.started_at = None
        self.ended_at = None
        self.elapsed_seconds = 0
        self.mine_count = mines
        self.flag_count = 0
        self.cells = [
            self._make_cell(row, column)
            for row in range(rows)
            for column in range(columns)
        ]

    def reveal_cell(
        self, row: int, column: int, now: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> None:
        """Reveal a hidden cell, laying out mines on the first reveal.

        Args:
            row: Row index of the target cell.
            column: Column index of the target cell.
            now: Optional ISO timestamp used as the current moment.

        Raises:
            InvalidActionError: If the game has already ended.
        """
        if self.status in ("won", "lost"):
            raise InvalidActionError(
                f"Cannot reveal a cell when the game is {self.status}."
            )
        moment = now if now is not None else self._now()
        rows, columns, _ = self._board_settings()
        if not self._in_bounds(row, column, rows, columns):
            return
        if self.status == "ready":
            self._lay_out_board(row, column)
            self.status = "in_progress"
            self.started_at = moment
        target = self._cell_at(row, column)
        if target is None or target["state"] != "hidden":
            return
        if target["has_mine"]:
            target["state"] = "revealed"
            self._expose_mines_on_loss()
            self._finish("lost", moment)
            return
        self._open_region(row, column, rows, columns)
        if all(
            cell["state"] == "revealed"
            for cell in self.cells
            if not cell["has_mine"]
        ):
            self._flag_remaining_mines()
            self._finish("won", moment)

    def toggle_flag(
        self, row: int, column: int, now: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> None:
        """Cycle a hidden cell to flagged or a flagged cell to hidden.

        Args:
            row: Row index of the target cell.
            column: Column index of the target cell.
            now: Optional ISO timestamp, accepted for interface symmetry.

        Raises:
            InvalidActionError: If the game has already ended.
        """
        if self.status not in ("ready", "in_progress"):
            raise InvalidActionError(
                f"Cannot flag a cell when the game is {self.status}."
            )
        cell = self._cell_at(row, column)
        if cell is None:
            return
        if cell["state"] == "hidden":
            cell["state"] = "flagged"
            self.flag_count += 1
        elif cell["state"] == "flagged":
            cell["state"] = "hidden"
            self.flag_count -= 1

    @staticmethod
    def _settings_for(difficulty: str) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
        if difficulty not in DIFFICULTY_SETTINGS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown difficulty: {difficulty}")
        return DIFFICULTY_SETTINGS[difficulty]

    def _board_settings(self) -> Tuple[int, int, int]:
        return self._settings_for(self.difficulty)

    @staticmethod
    def _in_bounds(row: int, column: int, rows: int, columns: int) -> bool:
        return 0 <= row < rows and 0 <= column < columns

    @staticmethod
    def _make_cell(
        row: int,
        column: int,
        state: str = "hidden",
        has_mine: bool = False,
        adjacent_mine_count: int = 0,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "id": f"{row}-{column}",
            "row": row,
            "column": column,
            "has_mine": has_mine,
            "adjacent_mine_count": adjacent_mine_count,
            "state": state,
        }

    @staticmethod
    def _neighbours(
        row: int, column: int, rows: int, columns: int
    ) -> List[Tuple[int, int]]:
        return [
            (r, c)
            for r in range(row - 1, row + 2)
            for c in range(column - 1, column + 2)
            if (r, c) != (row, column) and 0 <= r < rows and 0 <= c < columns
        ]

    def _cell_at(self, row: int, column: int) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
        for cell in self.cells:
            if cell["row"] == row and cell["column"] == column:
                return cell
        return None

    def _lay_out_board(self, row: int, column: int) -> None:
        rows, columns, mines = self._board_settings()
        self.mine_count = mines
        safe = {(row, column)} | set(
            self._neighbours(row, column, rows, columns)
        )
        candidates = [
            (r, c)
            for r in range(rows)
            for c in range(columns)
            if (r, c) not in safe
        ]
        mine_positions = set(random.sample(candidates, mines))
        self.cells = [
            self._make_cell(
                r,
                c,
                has_mine=(r, c) in mine_positions,
                adjacent_mine_count=sum(
                    1
                    for n in self._neighbours(r, c, rows, columns)
                    if n in mine_positions
                ),
            )
            for r in range(rows)
            for c in range(columns)
        ]

    def _open_region(self, row: int, column: int, rows: int, columns: int) -> None:
        pending = [(row, column)]
        while pending:
            r, c = pending.pop()
            cell = self._cell_at(r, c)
            if cell is None or cell["state"] != "hidden" or cell["has_mine"]:
                continue
            cell["state"] = "revealed"
            if cell["adjacent_mine_count"] == 0:
                pending.extend(self._neighbours(r, c, rows, columns))

    def _finish(self, outcome: str, ended: str) -> None:
        self.status = outcome
        self.ended_at = ended
        if self.started_at is not None:
            started = datetime.fromisoformat(self.started_at)
            finished = datetime.fromisoformat(ended)
            self.elapsed_seconds = int((finished - started).total_seconds())

    @staticmethod
    def _now() -> str:
        return datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()

    def mine_counter(self) -> int:
        """Return the mine counter, which may be negative.

        Returns:
            The mine count minus the flag count.
        """
        return self.mine_count - self.flag_count

    def timer_display(self) -> int:
        """Return the elapsed seconds capped for display.

        Returns:
            The elapsed seconds, never more than 999.
        """
        return min(self.elapsed_seconds, 999)

    def _expose_mines_on_loss(self) -> None:
        for cell in self.cells:
            if cell["has_mine"]:
                cell["state"] = "revealed"
            elif cell["state"] == "flagged":
                cell["state"] = "wrong"

    def _flag_remaining_mines(self) -> None:
        for cell in self.cells:
            if cell["has_mine"] and cell["state"] == "hidden":
                cell["state"] = "flagged"
                self.flag_count += 1

Keep the shape the object has when it is newly created: a collection that starts with one item for every position (each cell of a grid, each slot of a day) keeps one item for every position, each with every key the class's description lists, and you change only what the items hold. Reach a situation through a sequence of calls only when the scenario is about that sequence itself. ## Rules
1. Write ONE pytest test module that verifies the scenario's behavior: arrange (Given), act (When), assert (Then).
2. Construct the object using ONLY fields that appear in the current API, and pass every field that has no default. Never invent constructor arguments. If the scenario needs a field that does not exist yet, set it as an attribute after construction.
3. If the scenario needs behavior that does not exist yet, call it the way the scenario implies. A missing method (AttributeError) or a failed assertion is the expected RED outcome. Choose clear method and keyword-argument names: the implementer will be given this test and will implement exactly that interface.
4. When the scenario says an operation is rejected or raises, use `with pytest.raises(Exception) as exc_info:` and assert `type(exc_info.value).__name__ == "<Name>"`, where the name is the one the interface above gives for that kind of refusal, or, when it gives none, the name the scenario implies. Never import exception classes from the domain module. Compare a field against the values the interface above lists for it, spelled exactly so.
5. Use fixed, explicit values (fixed ISO datetimes, plain numbers). Never call `datetime.now()` and never depend on the clock: pass reference times as arguments.
6. Forbidden: `hasattr`, `getattr`, `inspect`, mocking the class under test, `assert True`, and tests that only check that something exists or returns True without the scenario's input.
7. When the scenario states a number or limit, test BOTH sides of that boundary: one case just beyond it (rejected/invalid, e.g. 119 for a 120 minimum) and one case exactly at it (accepted/valid, e.g. exactly 120). Write them as two test functions or one `pytest.mark.parametrize`. The accepted case must call the same operation and assert it succeeds (no exception, and the resulting state). For rules about ranges, intervals or overlap, also test two intervals that merely touch at an endpoint (end equals start), and state whether the scenario treats that as an overlap.
8. When the scenario's rule holds alike for each of several parties, sides or kinds the class knows (each party, each role, each direction), test it for at least two of them, as separate test functions or one `pytest.mark.parametrize`: an implementation written out once per party is only proved for the parties a test reaches.
9. When the scenario says what is allowed (which transitions or values a thing may take), also test one case the rule does not allow, the kind nearest to an allowed one, and assert it is refused: a rule proved only by what it permits is also met by an implementation that permits everything.
10. Build each refused case from an accepted one by changing only what the rule is about, and keep everything else the same: as many items, as many steps taken, the same amounts and the same history length. Then nothing but the rule can tell the two cases apart, and an implementation that goes by something easier to count (how many steps were taken, how many items exist) fails one of them.

```python
from src.domain.game import Game


STARTED = "2024-01-01T10:00:00+00:00"
WON_AT = "2024-01-01T10:05:00+00:00"


def make_cell(row, column, has_mine, adjacent_mine_count, state):
    return {
        "id": f"r{row}c{column}",
        "row": row,
        "column": column,
        "has_mine": has_mine,
        "adjacent_mine_count": adjacent_mine_count,
        "state": state,
    }


def build_in_progress_game_one_safe_cell_left():
    # 2x2 region of the board. Mine at (0,0). Safe cells (0,1), (1,0), (1,1).
    # Each safe cell touches the mine at (0,0) (edge-adjacent or diagonal),
    # so each has adjacent_mine_count 1, which means no zero-count expansion.
    # (0,1) and (1,0) are already revealed; (1,1) is still hidden.
    # No flags are placed, so flag_count is 0.
    # started_at is an ISO timestamp with an explicit offset, matching the
    # offset-aware reference time passed to reveal_cell.
    game = Game(id="game-1")
    game.status = "in_progress"
    game.started_at = STARTED
    game.ended_at = None
    game.elapsed_seconds = 0
    game.mine_count = 1
    game.flag_count = 0
    game.cells = [
        make_cell(0, 0, True, 0, "hidden"),
        make_cell(0, 1, False, 1, "revealed"),
        make_cell(1, 0, False, 1, "revealed"),
        make_cell(1, 1, False, 1, "hidden"),
    ]
    return game


def get_cell(game, row, column):
    matches = [c for c in game.cells if c["row"] == row and c["column"] == column]
    assert len(matches) == 1
    return matches[0]


def test_revealing_last_safe_cell_wins_and_flags_remaining_mines():
    # Given an in-progress game where the only hidden safe cell is (1,1),
    # the mine at (0,0) is still hidden, and the session started at STARTED.
    game = build_in_progress_game_one_safe_cell_left()

    # When the last non-mine cell (1,1) is revealed at the moment WON_AT.
    # Revealing (1,1) is a hidden, unflagged, safe cell on an in-progress game,
    # so the reveal is accepted. Once it is opened, every non-mine cell
    # (0,1), (1,0), (1,1) is revealed, so the session is won.
    game.reveal_cell(row=1, column=1, now=WON_AT)

    # Then the status becomes "won", because every non-mine cell is revealed.
    assert game.status == "won"

    # And ended_at is set to the moment the session ended.
    assert game.ended_at == WON_AT

    # And the timer stops at the win: 5 minutes after STARTED is 300 seconds.
    assert game.elapsed_seconds == 300

    # And the unrevealed mine at (0,0) becomes flagged on the win,
    # since it was hidden when the session was won.
    assert get_cell(game, 0, 0)["state"] == "flagged"

    # And the safe cells keep their revealed state.
    assert get_cell(game, 0, 1)["state"] == "revealed"
    assert get_cell(game, 1, 0)["state"] == "revealed"
    assert get_cell(game, 1, 1)["state"] == "revealed"
```
